subject: ss-gastroenterology
title: Colorectal Polyps, Hereditary Syndromes and Screening

steps.tx: The classical adenoma-carcinoma sequence, or chromosomal instability pathway, causes approximately eighty percent of sporadic colorectal cancers. Driven by the orderly sequential accumulation of somatic mutations, the initiation event is the biallelic inactivation of the **adenomatous polyposis coli** tumor suppressor gene located on chromosome **5**q21. Loss of APC impairs beta-catenin degradation, leading to nuclear accumulation and constitutive activation of c-MYC and cyclin D1.

steps.tx: The serrated neoplasia pathway accounts for fifteen to twenty percent of colorectal cancers, originating from sessile serrated lesions predominantly located in the right colon. These lesions are characterized by early activating **BRAF** mutations, specifically the V600E substitution. Subsequent extensive aberrant hypermethylation of promoter CpG islands, designated the **CpG island methylator phenotype**, silences the DNA mismatch repair gene **MLH1**, precipitating high microsatellite instability (MSI-H) and rapid carcinogenesis.

steps.tx: **Lynch syndrome**, or hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer, is an autosomal dominant condition caused by germline mutations in **DNA mismatch repair** genes. The primary genes involved include **MLH1**, **MSH2**, **MSH6**, and **PMS2**, as well as EPCAM deletions that cause epigenetic silencing of MSH2. Defective mismatch repair prevents the correction of replication slippage errors, causing high microsatellite instability and predisposing to right-sided colorectal, endometrial, ovarian, and gastric carcinomas.

steps.tx: Clinical identification of families with suspected Lynch syndrome uses the **Amsterdam II criteria**, encapsulated by the **3-2-1** rule: at least **3** relatives with histologically confirmed Lynch-associated cancers, spanning at least **2** successive generations, with at least **1** case diagnosed before age **50** years. Furthermore, one affected individual must be a first-degree relative of the other two, familial adenomatous polyposis must be ruled out, and tumors must be verified pathologically.

steps.tx: Classical **familial adenomatous polyposis** is an autosomal dominant syndrome resulting from germline mutations in the APC gene on chromosome 5q21. It is defined clinically by the development of hundreds to thousands of colorectal adenomatous polyps, traditionally exceeding a diagnostic threshold of at least **100** adenomas. Without prophylactic surgical intervention, the lifetime risk of developing invasive colorectal adenocarcinoma approaches **100%** by the fourth to fifth decade of life.

steps.tx: Colorectal surveillance protocols in confirmed Lynch syndrome carriers mandate regular high-quality colonoscopy with targeted biopsies. High-level consensus guidelines recommend initiating screening colonoscopy between the ages of **20** and **25** years, or 2 to 5 years earlier than the youngest affected family member. Surveillance must be repeated at strict intervals of every **1** to **2** years due to accelerated adenoma-carcinoma dwell times driven by defective DNA mismatch repair.

steps.tx: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is an autosomal dominant hamartomatous polyposis condition caused by germline inactivating mutations in the serine/threonine kinase gene **STK11** (also designated **LKB1**) located on chromosome 19p13.3. Patients develop distinctive mucocutaneous melanin pigmentation on the lips, buccal mucosa, and digits. Gastrointestinal polyps are **hamartomatous**, characterized histopathologically by arborizing smooth muscle proliferation extending into the mucosal lamina propria.

left.title: Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome
points: Polyp histology: Hamartomas with arborizing smooth muscle
Mucocutaneous: Hyperpigmented macules on lips and buccal mucosa
Associated malignancies: Breast, pancreas, GI, ovarian (SCTAT)

right.title: Juvenile Polyposis Syndrome
points: Polyp histology: Dilated cystic glands with lamina propria edematous expansion
Associated malignancies: Colorectal and gastric adenocarcinoma

steps.tx: For average-risk asymptomatic populations, international guidelines recommend initiating routine **colorectal cancer screening** at age **45** years. The clinical gold standard is **colonoscopy** performed every **10** years. For screening programs utilizing non-invasive modalities, the fecal immunochemical test (**FIT**) is performed **annually**, detecting human globin to trigger diagnostic colonoscopy upon positive findings.
